comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Reporting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company adopted FASB ASU 2023-07 in the fourth quarter of 2024 to enhance disclosures about significant segment expenses, as this standard was effective for fiscal year 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose the impact of FASB ASU 2023-07 on segment reporting. Both companies reference the issuance in November 2023 and the standard's focus on enhancing disclosures about significant segment expenses. However, they differ in implementation status for fiscal year 2024: AMD adopted the standard in the fourth quarter of 2024 as it was effective for that fiscal year, whereas MU states the standard is effective for its 2025 annual reporting and will not impact its 2024 financial statements, only its future disclosures.

sentences.text: In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") 2023-07 (ASC Topic 280), Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures.
This ASU expands on existing reportable segment disclosure requirements primarily through enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses.
This ASU is effective for our annual reporting for 2025 on a retrospective basis.

In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standard Update (ASU) 2023-07 Segment Reporting (Topic 280) Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures to enhance disclosures about significant segment expenses.
This ASU is effective for the Company's fiscal year 2024 and interim periods in fiscal year 2025.
The Company adopted this standard in the fourth quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of FASB Operating Segment Disclosure Standard
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is evaluating the impact of a new FASB standard issued in November 2023 requiring additional disclosures about significant expenses in operating segments, which is effective retrospectively for the annual reporting period of fiscal year 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA discuss the adoption of the new FASB standard issued in November 2023 regarding additional disclosures about significant expenses in operating segments. Both companies identify the effective period for annual reporting as fiscal year 2025. NVDA states it is currently evaluating the impact of the standard, while MU explicitly states the standard will impact its disclosures but not its financial statements, confirming alignment on the retrospective application scope for FY2025 reporting.

sentences.text: In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") 2023-07 (ASC Topic 280), Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures.
This ASU expands on existing reportable segment disclosure requirements primarily through enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses.
This ASU is effective for our annual reporting for 2025 on a retrospective basis.
This standard will impact our disclosures and will not impact our financial statements.
In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board, or FASB, issued a new accounting standard to provide for additional disclosures about significant expenses in operating segments.
The standard is effective for our annual reporting for fiscal year 2025 and for interim period reporting starting in fiscal year 2026 retrospectively.
We are currently evaluating the impact of this standard on our Consolidated Financial Statements.
